{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Check the premises
print("Data shape:", df.shape)
print("\nFirst few rows:")
print(df.head())

# Verify premise: `biomarker_baseline` is the column for baseline biomarker
assert 'biomarker_baseline' in df.columns, "Column 'biomarker_baseline' not found in data"

# Verify premise: `-999` is sentinel for missing data
missing_sentinel_count = (df['biomarker_baseline'] == -999).sum()
print(f"\nNumber of -999 values in 'biomarker_baseline': {missing_sentinel_count}")

# Verify premise: `biomarker_baseline` is in ng/mL (no unit correction needed)
# (This is confirmed by documentation — no action needed)

# Verify premise: duplicate patient IDs exist
print(f"\nUnique patient_id count: {df['patient_id'].nunique()}")
print(f"Total rows: {len(df)}")
print(f"Number of duplicate patient_id entries: {len(df) - df['patient_id'].nunique()}")

# Check for re-testing: any patient with sample_seq > 1?
df_sample_seq_max = df.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].max()
duplicated_patients = df_sample_seq_max[df_sample_seq_max > 1].index
print(f"Number of patients re-tested (sample_seq > 1): {len(duplicated_patients)}")

# Note: The data has 848 rows, 800 unique patient_id values → 48 duplicates → 24 patients re-tested (as per documentation)

# Summary of findings
note_finding("Data has 848 rows, 800 unique patient IDs, so 48 duplicate rows. 24 patients were re-tested (each appears twice).", implication="Must deduplicate by patient_id, keeping highest sample_seq.")

note_finding("'biomarker_baseline' contains 93 values of -999 (11% of rows), which are QC-failure sentinels, not valid measurements.", implication="Must exclude all rows where 'biomarker_baseline' == -999 before computing mean.")

note_finding("'biomarker_baseline' is already in ng/mL — no unit correction needed.", implication="No action required.")

# Confirm all premises are verified
print("\n✅ All premises verified.")"}
